goal: Add a --quiet flag to the sample project's CLI that suppresses progress output but never suppresses errors, and prove it with a smoke run.

dod: a smoke run with --quiet produces no progress lines on stdout
a smoke run with --quiet still prints an error to stderr on bad input
the full unit suite is green
milestones.title: Flag implemented and smoke-proven

rationale: The only order whose DoD cannot be satisfied by pytest alone: the feature must be exercised through the app's real entry point. It probes the smoke runner and the difference between 'the code is right' and 'the product does it' — a distinction unit tests structurally cannot make.
title: Add a user-visible flag whose proof is a smoke run, not a unit test
